p:cNvPr.descr: The steps and materials involved in next-generation pyrosequencing. (a) At the top of the diagram is a template DNA strand and a primer DNA strand on top. The primer begins with 5’, while the template begins with 3’. The nitrogenous bases are represented by colored shapes with the appropriate letter symbol inside. A is blue, G is green, C is red, and T is yellow. From left to right, the sequence of the template strand is TCCAGCAAGT. The primer strand sequence, from left to right, is AGGTC. Above this image are three A units, labeled above with text reading, “pulse in dATP”. An arrow points down from the A units to the primer strand. Below the template and primer is a down arrow with a text box on the right reading, “No flash of light; dATP degraded by apyrase.” Below this is text reading, “pulse in dGTP,” with 3 G units below. An arrow points down from the G units to the primer strand, which has the same structure and sequence as previously described. A down arrow has a text box to the right that reads, “Base is incorporated; pyrophosphate is released.” Below this are 2 phosphate groups bonded together, shown as 2 white circles with the letter P inside. Below the phosphate groups is another down arrow, with a text box on the right reading, “Sulfurylase uses pyrophosphate to convert adenosine 5’-phosphosulfate into ATP.” A curved arrow transverses this down arrow from left to right. On the left end is an image of a blue A unit bonded right to a gray pentagon, which bonds right to a phosphate group, which bonds right to a sulfate, represented by a circled S. Following the arrow right, we see that the S has separated from the adenosine-5’-phosphosulfate. Another down arrow shows the A unit bonded right to the gray pentagon, which bonds right to 3 phosphate groups (ATP). To the right there is a text box reading, “In the presence of ATP, luciferase reacts with luciferin.” A down arrow points to a bright yellow region with the words “flash of light”. Below there is a graph showing the nucleotide sequence. The vertical axis is labeled “relative light intensity” and has a range of 0-2, with interval 1. The top horizontal axis is labeled “nucleotide sequence” and reads, from left to right, AGGTC(large space)GTTCAG. The bottom horizontal axis is labeled “nucleotide added” with the sequence, from left to right, AGCTAGTCAG. There are red peaks indicating the intensity of a particular nucleotide at a given point on the sequence. From the left: A has intensity 1, G/GG has intensity 2; T and C have intensity 1. A has no peak in the center of the horizontal axes; G has intensity 1, T has intensity 2; C, A, & G all have intensity 1. (b) Illustration of a DNA sequencing run, shown with clusters of DNA fragments. The sequencing run is a row of small black boxes which contain white dots representing DNA fragments. On the left end is text reading, “DNA sequence at circled clusters.” There is a line below this text, and 2 sequences just below this. The top sequence reads AGTTCGTTCAG:. The bottom sequence has 3 underscores (blanks) to the left of the sequence: CAGTTCAG. At the top is a bracket spanning the length of the row, with text reading, “dNTP added.” The black boxes have letters on top corresponding to the nucleotides. In the black boxes there are white dots that represent lit-up DNA fragment clusters. Each box has 2 spots circled, one for the top sequence and one for the bottom. The bottom circles for A, T, and G at the far left have no white dots. Text at the bottom reads: “Duplicate dNTP incorporation results in 2x brighter flash.” Pointer lines indicate the brightest flashes; 2 at the rightmost T and 1 at top of the leftmost G.
